claim_boundary: Primary evidence identifies Cboe SKEW as a risk-neutral left-tail measure that is low-correlated with and complementary to VIX. Cross-market Bitcoin evidence supports time-varying traditional-risk transmission but not a stable SKEW timing rule. Exactly one preregistered long-or-cash historical audit may test whether avoiding only the highest lagged SKEW states improves BTC risk-adjusted economics. Failure closes this exact tail-risk percentile family without changing source, lag, lookback, relation or thresholds.

feature_contract.formula: midrank percentile of the latest Cboe SKEW close against exactly the preceding 252 Cboe business-day closes

independence_contract.not_vix_rescue: The feature is risk-neutral third-moment asymmetry, not the VIX variance level, slope, threshold, smoothing or BTC interaction. Cboe reports low variation correlation between SKEW and VIX and describes SKEW as an additional tail-risk layer.

prior_matrix.finding: Cboe defines SKEW from S&P 500 option prices as a 30-day risk-neutral skewness measure that rises with perceived negative tail risk, reports low correlation with VIX variations, and positions it as a complementary tail-risk layer.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: An equity-option tail-risk price is not proof that it forecasts Bitcoin or that a long-or-cash implementation improves economics.

prior_matrix.identity: Yae and Tian, Volatile safe-haven asset: Evidence from Bitcoin (2024)
prior_matrix.finding: The study reports that time-varying Bitcoin and S&P 500 correlation contains next-day Bitcoin return information, supporting a possible cross-market risk-transmission channel.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Correlation-state predictability does not identify SKEW, an 80th-percentile rule, execution feasibility, costs or risk-adjusted performance.

prior_matrix.identity: Stremmel, What can monetary policy tell us about Bitcoin? (2023)
prior_matrix.finding: Bitcoin reacts to traditional monetary and market information, but the magnitude and sign vary over time and simple stable return relations are unclear.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Time variation requires separate Design and Validation, annual breadth, concentration visibility and neighbor stability rather than reliance on an aggregate relation.

real_time_design_requirements: Use only the committed Cboe daily SKEW subset and exactly the prior 252 available Cboe business-day closes.
Make each SKEW close effective no earlier than 00:00 UTC on the following calendar day and persist its state across weekends and holidays.
Freeze primary percentile 0.8 and neighbors 0.7 and 0.9 before BTC outcome access.
Use a spot-only 100-percent BTC or 100-percent cash policy with next-H1-open fills, explicit normal and doubled stress friction, realized/unrealized separation and terminal liquidation.
Require positive Design and Validation economics, drawdown and Calmar improvement, upside capture, annual breadth, concentration control and both-neighbor stability.
Do not add an absolute SKEW threshold, different lookback, smoothing, VIX combination, BTC interaction, partial sizing, leverage, shorting or threshold search after outcome access.
Do not open post-2024 OOS or create a Trading runtime rule from this audit.
uncertainty: SKEW measures S&P 500 option-implied left-tail pricing, not crypto-specific tail risk, and its Bitcoin transfer may be weak or regime-dependent.
High SKEW may represent priced insurance demand or a risk premium rather than an immediately avoidable BTC drawdown state.
The 252-business-day percentile normalizes secular index levels but may still vary across monetary, option-market and Bitcoin-adoption regimes.
Cboe historical data is informational and mutable at its public endpoint; only the exact committed bytes and response revision identity are evidence for this audit.
No BTC performance result, post-2024 data, OOS, candidate, runtime filter or Trading path was accessed while freezing this prior.
